notes: Governing documents saved: the 2016-2019 Collective Agreement (Part 3 Art. 6 Maternity and Parental Leave; Art. 1 tenure clock; Arts. 4, 7 leaves) and Policy 62 (sick leave). The no-policy coding (`missing`) does not apply; missing = false.

Structure: the CA states no leave length of its own; Art. 6.06 refers to the Employment Standards Act, and the HR page states the ESA leaves (17 + 35 for a birth mother; 37 for a birth father or adopting parent). The leaves are coded as the statute (c1-c4); UBC's SEB top-ups and waiting-week pay are pay within them (checklist §5 ex. 1, S1, R18).

EI waiting period: CA 6.01/6.02 were written for a 2-week EI waiting period; the CA's 2017 note (EI changes effective 2017-01-01) keeps SEB at 95% during the second week 'in addition to the EI benefit'. Coded as stages: one waiting week at 95% (c5; c10 for a parent who has not served it), then SEB top-up while EI is received (c6 15 weeks; c9 10 weeks). Matches the HR table and FA page (16 weeks maternity incl. the waiting week; 10 weeks parental for the birth mother; 11 incl. the waiting week for the partner). CA 6.03's '27 weeks' total reflects the old 2-week wait.

Chain, birth parent: ESA pregnancy leave 17 (c1; waiting-week pay wk 1 c5, SEB top-up wks 2-16 c6, EI maternity from wk 2 c7) -> ESA recovery extension 6 (c2, if certified) -> ESA parental 35 (c3; SEB parental top-up 10 within it, c9) -> child's-condition extension 5 (c4). Benefits: EI maternity 15 (c7) -> EI parental 35 (c8).
Chain, non-birth parent: ESA parental 37 (c3; waiting-week pay wk 1 c10, SEB top-up 10 from wk 2 c9, EI parental 35 from wk 2 c8) -> child's-condition extension 5 (c4).

FA Leaves page (marked 'under review') says birth mothers are entitled to 16 weeks of maternity leave (CA Part 3 Art. 6); the CA states no leave length and the ESA gives 17. Not coded separately; the '16 weeks' matches the SEB period (1 + 15).

Tenure clock: HR page says the one-year extension is automatic for 'maternity or parental leave'; CA 1.03 makes it automatic for maternity leave and on request for any parent by birth or adoption. The CA governs (c12 flagged conflicting_sources). Whether c11 and c12 can both apply to a birth mother is not stated.

Study-leave eligibility credit (CA Part 3 2.01(a): up to six months of sick, maternity or parental leave counts as full-time service; HR: up to 27 weeks with SUB top-up) is not a leave, pay, relief or protection for the birth; not a component.

Not components (not usable for a birth): study leave (CA Part 3 Art. 2), leave for improving basic qualifications (Art. 3), leave at the request of the University (Art. 5), Heads' administrative leave (Part 4 1.03), retirement options (Part 1 LOU 2, age 60+).

Other groups recorded in notes only: staff sick-leave banks and postdoctoral-fellow sick leave (HR sick page); Academic Executive sick leave (Policy 62, up to six months; excluded from the bargaining unit); graduate-student provisions on the Science page (NSERC/CIHR eligibility cases, CUPE 2278 Hardship Maternity Fund, four-year fellowship holders); HR page pages for staff groups (not saved). Postdoctoral fellows (employees) receive EI and SEB like faculty (same HR page).

Faculty of Science provisions (c26, c27) are unit-level (V3b, V3c): recorded, not counted. The 2009 principles add dean's-office cover for adoptive parents' reductions; the 2018 page restates the rest.
Unpaid general leave beyond the ESA (HR: 26 weeks birth mother, 24 birth father, if requested and approved) is the CA Art. 4 leave without pay (c22), general purpose and discretionary.

Documents cited but not saved: Senior Manager, Health, Wellbeing & Benefit's email of 2016-12-19 (CA 2017 note); Leave of Absence Agreement (FA page; appears to be CA Part 3); UBC Policy 42, 61, 85, 86, 3; HR pages: Benefits Coverage while on a Leave, General Leave, Unpaid Sick Leave, Maternity/Parental/Adoption Leave for other employee groups and for Postdoctoral Fellows (Award Recipients); Income Replacement Plan terms; NSERC/CIHR parental leave policies and check list; UBC Graduate Studies leave policy; UBC Science Parental Leave Report 2004; Faculty of Science departmental policies; Maternity/Parental/Adoption Leave Application form (postdocs).
